text: Continuous integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code changes to a shared repository, and an automated system builds the project each time. This process is called automated builds. The CI pipeline then runs tests automatically to check that everything works correctly. Because problems are found quickly, teams can catch issues early before they become serious. A good CI pipeline saves time and reduces stress, since developers do not need to test everything by hand. As a result, software is released faster and with fewer bugs, which makes both the team and the users happier.
